summary: The Judeo-Arabic was read word by word. Errors found: 'attributed to him' for אלי' (ilā), a passive for the active פנסבה, 'one' for 'we' in נסתדל, and the wrong sense of אלמפתעלה ('forged'). In the Hebrew: 'embellishments' for גיזומים, 'a blind and insipid man' for the Ezekiel idiom טח תפל, 'read' for 'called' (the pun on Matzref), the missed echo of Deut 17:11 in ימין ושמאל, שבתך as a verb, and 'Rabbi' dropped from the author's heading. Three questions on ממש, עבודה in the Haggadah verse, and אמנתא. Apparatus, grammar and readings were rewritten.

patches.value: §12. Behold, then, surely all your words are exaggerations and hyperboles, to alarm the fools and the madmen who love wonders and impossibilities, and you speak without knowledge. And all your words are without reason. And in deceit you refuse to know the LORD, as the prophet Jeremiah, peace be upon him, said in the name of the LORD: "Your dwelling is in the midst of deceit; through deceit they have refused to know Me, declares the LORD." And already one of the deceivers among you has said: "We know that the truth is with you." But what business is it of yours to reveal this matter and to publicize it to some of the students. It would be better for you to leave them in their error entirely, as the words of the wicked one among the four sons, who says: "What is this service to you? etc." And the proof that you daub whitewash: for in this letter of yours you published that the Rabbi, the author of Matzref ha-Emunah, is, God forbid, a heretic and a denier. And you called his book Mesharef ha-Emunah. And he, in his integrity, walks without turning aside from the words of the Zohar, and Mikdash Melekh, and Kisse Eliyahu, and the RaShB, and Yosher Levav, and Sefer ha-Berit, and Rabbi the Ari, and Rabbi Chayyim Vital in the book Etz Chayyim, and Nachalat Yosef, and their finest flour, to the right or to the left. As will be explained below, and first I will bring you several proofs. This Kabbalah is not a halakhah given to Moses at Sinai, for our Rabbis of blessed memory said in Eruvin: "Any baraita that is not taught in the house of Rabbi Oshaya, it is not a baraita, and you may not object from it, for it is corrupted." Thus, any baraita that did not enter the study-house of Rabbi Chiyya or of Rabbi Oshaya, not only is it not a halakhah given to Moses at Sinai. But one may not even raise an objection from it against an Amora. And in the Yerushalmi, Eruvin, chapter one, in the passage de-Lechayyim, it is written. And these are his words: "Acha said to him: So said Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish: any mishnah that did not enter the fellowship, one does not rely on it." Thus far. And see below, §42. And in an old notebook of the compositions of our forefathers I found written in the name of Rabbi Saadia Gaon, and these are his words: "The book Shiur Komah: no trustworthy transmission has come down concerning it, for it is not in the Mishnah and not in the Talmud. And there is no proof by which we can infer whether Rabbi Ishmael truly said it, or another said it and ascribed it to him, as many of the forged books are ascribed to some of the famous scholars." Thus far his words. (Translation by the Rabbi, the author: "The book Shiur Komah: we have no tradition concerning it from the sages of our faith, since it is neither in the Mishnah nor in the Talmud, and also there is no proof to be drawn from it whether Rabbi Ishmael truly said it, or others besides him said it and ascribed it to Rabbi Ishmael, as they ascribe many of the books that were made to some of the famous sages.")
patches.reason: Several errors: גיזומים (gozma) is hyperbole, not 'embellishments'; Jer 9:5 שבתך is a noun ('your dwelling'), not a verb; 'טח תפל' is the idiom of Ezek 13:10 (daubing whitewash), not 'a blind man'; וקראת את ספרו משרף is 'you called his book Mesharef' (the pun on Matzref), not 'read'; ימין ושמאל completes לא סר (Deut 17:11); the Arabic is 'we can infer', 'ascribed it to him' (active, object suffix), and 'the forged books ... to some famous scholars' (אלי' is ilā, not ilayhi), so 'attributed to him' is an error; the Hebrew heading is 'Translation by the Rabbi, the author'; 'that' before 'all your words', 'but first' for ותחלה, 'it goes without saying' for לא מיבעיא ... אלא דאפילו, and 'made for' are not exact.

patches.reason: The corrected English changed the phrases.

patches.value: The ש is not carried by an English 'that': 'surely all your words are ...'.
patches.reason: 'Behold, then, surely that all your words are' has no main clause.

patches.value: and hyperboles
patches.reason: גיזומים from גוזמא, 'hyperbole, exaggeration' (Aramaic); not 'embellishments'.

patches.value: Literal 'cuttings'; גוזמא in the Talmud is the word for hyperbole, set beside הפלגות as a second word for exaggeration.
patches.reason: The old note contradicted the gloss and the sense.

patches.value: your dwelling
patches.reason: שבתך (Jer 9:5) is the noun 'your dwelling', with no verb in the verse.

patches.value: שִׁבְתְּךָ in the verse is a noun ('your sitting, dwelling'); the verse has no verb: 'Your dwelling is in the midst of deceit'.
patches.reason: Jer 9:5.

patches.value: ממש is placed after בטעותם but may belong with כדברי ('exactly as the words of the wicked one'). Question: read 'in their error, exactly as the words of the wicked one among the four sons' (proposed) rather than 'in their error entirely'. See readings.
patches.reason: The scope of ממש is open; the rulings are silent. Proposed ruling: attach ממש to כדברי ('exactly as'), the usual idiom, with the other reading in readings.

patches.value: Question: Exod 12:26, the verse the Haggadah's wicked son speaks, has עבודה for the Passover rite. The rulings fix 'worship' for עבודה of God or gods and 'serve' for a human master, and are silent on a rite. Proposed ruling: keep 'service' here with this note, and record 'worship' in readings.
patches.reason: Rulings on עבודה do not cover the Passover rite; proposed 'service' for the rite.

patches.value: daub
patches.reason: טח is the participle of טוח, 'to daub, plaster' (Ezek 13:10, 22:28), not 'blind'.

patches.value: טח: 'daubing' (plastering a wall). The pair טח תפל echoes Ezek 13:10 and 22:28, the false prophets who daub a wall with whitewash: speech that covers the flaw with a flimsy coat.
patches.reason: Wrong sense and a missed allusion.

patches.value: whitewash
patches.reason: תפל in Ezek 13:10 is whitewash (untempered mortar).

patches.value: תפל: whitewash, untempered mortar (Ezek 13:10); the same word also means 'insipid, unsalted'.
patches.reason: As above.

patches.value: Matzref ha-Emunah: 'the refining of faith', from צרף, 'refine'. It is the title of the Rabbi's book.
patches.reason: 'the book the author defends' is not in the Hebrew.

patches.value: and you called
patches.reason: וקראת את ספרו משרף: 'you called his book Mesharef' (קרא with two objects); the pun on Matzref is the point.

patches.value: Mesharef ha-Emunah: 'the burning of faith', from שרף, 'burn'. The interlocutor's name for the book, a pun on Matzref (3:12.88).
patches.reason: With 'called' the note reads true.

patches.value: סולתם: 'their fine flour', that is, the best of them. With ימין ושמאל it completes לא סר: 'has not turned aside ... to the right or to the left' (Deut 17:11; Josh 1:7).
patches.reason: The old note cut ימין ושמאל off from לא סר.

patches.value: to the right
patches.reason: ימין ושמאל after לא סר echoes Deut 17:11.

patches.value: or to the left
patches.reason: As above.

patches.value: and first
patches.reason: ותחלה has ו, 'and'; 'but' adds an adversative.

patches.value: into the house of
patches.reason: With 164 the phrase is בית מדרשו, 'the study-house of'; the old glosses doubled 'house'.

patches.value: his study
patches.reason: מדרשו 'his study'; בית מדרשו = 'the study-house of'.

patches.value: בית מדרשו של: literally 'the house of his study of'; English 'the study-house of'.
patches.reason: Doubling.

patches.value: not
patches.reason: לא מיבעיא ... אלא דאפילו: 'not only ... but even'.

patches.value: only
patches.reason: As above.

patches.value: לא מיבעיא: Aramaic, literally 'it is not needed to ask'; with אלא דאפילו it means 'not only ... but even'.
patches.reason: The pair needs 'not only'.

patches.value: Question: אמנתא is read as amāna(tan), 'trustworthy' (a reliable transmission). The author's Hebrew has מחכמי אמונתנו, 'the sages of our faith', which suggests amānatinā ('of our faith'). Proposed ruling: keep 'trustworthy' as the Arabic stands and give 'transmission of our faith' in readings and apparatus.
patches.reason: Ambiguous spelling: the ruling is to translate the evident word, note it and record the alternative.

patches.value: אר: evidently a scribal ר for ד, that is אד (idh), 'since, because'. Translated 'for'. Alternative: none that fits.
patches.reason: The old note passed over the odd spelling.

patches.value: we infer
patches.reason: נסתדל is first person plural (nastadill), 'we infer, draw proof'; the old note gave yastadill 'one'.

patches.value: Judeo-Arabic nastadill, from istadalla, 'to infer, argue': 'we can infer'. The nun is the first-person plural prefix.
patches.reason: Person.

patches.value: by it
patches.reason: בה bihi, 'by it', the proof.

patches.value: עלי׳ is עלי, ʿalā 'in, upon', with a geresh marking the alif maqsura (written yod); it is not 'him'. עלי׳ אלחקיקה = 'in truth'.
patches.reason: Explains the spelling the translator read correctly.

patches.value: and ascribed it
patches.reason: פנסבה = fa-nasabahu: the object suffix ה makes the verb active ('and ascribed it'), parallel to the Hebrew וייחסו; not passive.

patches.value: to him
patches.reason: אליה ilayhi.

patches.value: תנסב: passive (tunsab), 'are ascribed'.
patches.reason: Contrast with the active verb at 3:12.258.

patches.value: forged
patches.reason: אלמפתעלה = al-muftaʿala, 'the forged, fabricated'; the Hebrew העשויים 'made'.

patches.value: Literally 'fabricated, invented' (iftaʿala); a book forged in the name of an authority.
patches.reason: Old note 'attributed' was wrong.

patches.value: to
patches.reason: אלי׳ = ilā, 'to' (the geresh marks the alif maqsura), not ilayhi 'to him'. 'Attributed to him' was invented.

patches.value: some
patches.reason: בעץ baʿḍ 'some'.

patches.value: העשויים: 'made'; the Arabic has 'forged'. The Hebrew order 'ascribe many of the books that were made to some of the famous sages' may also be read 'books made in the name of some of the sages'; see readings.
patches.reason: 'made for' misconstrued לקצת.

patches.value: לקצת: 'to some', the sages to whom the books are ascribed.
patches.reason: As above.

value: Section label §12 (token 1). 'Behold, then, surely all your words are exaggerations and hyperboles': הפלגות and גיזומים (גוזמא) both name exaggeration; 'to alarm' (להבהיל) gives the purpose.
Jer 9:5 is quoted after כמאמר ... בשם ה'. שבתך is a noun, 'your dwelling'; מאנו is a perfect, 'have refused'.

שאתה טח תפל echoes Ezek 13:10 and 22:28 (daubing whitewash on a wall): 'you daub whitewash'. וקראת את ספרו משרף האמונה: קרא takes two objects, 'you called his book Mesharef ha-Emunah', a pun on Matzref ha-Emunah.

לא סר ... ימין ושמאל echoes Deut 17:11 and Josh 1:7: he has not turned aside, to the right or to the left, from the Zohar and the other works and their finest flour. לא מיבעיא ... אלא דאפילו is Aramaic 'not only ... but even'.

The Eruvin passage is Bavli Aramaic; the Yerushalmi passage is Yerushalmi Aramaic and has no verb in the Hebrew, so 'it is written' supplies the main clause. The Haggadah words are from Exod 12:26, given with וכו'.

Judeo-Arabic (Saadia): the geresh in עלי׳ and אלי׳ marks the alif maqsura (ʿalā 'in', ilā 'to'); אליה is ilayhi 'to him'. אר is a slip for אד (idh) 'since'. נסתדל is first person plural 'we infer'. פנסבה carries an object suffix: 'and ascribed it'; תנסב is passive 'are ascribed'. The author's Hebrew in parentheses is translated from the Hebrew.
patches.reason: Rewritten for the corrected readings; the Arabic points are needed by a learner.

value: Base text from Wikisource; collation with the 1931 scan not yet made (open question 2).
Jer 9:5, quoted by the author: 'שבתך בתוך מרמה במרמה מאנו דעת אותי נאם ה''.
Exod 12:26 (the verse the wicked son speaks in the Haggadah): 'מה העבודה הזאת לכם'; the author gives it with וכו'.
Ezek 13:10 (also 22:28): 'וטחים אתו תפל', allusion in 'אתה טח תפל'.
Deut 17:11 (also Josh 1:7): 'לא תסור ... ימין ושמאל', allusion in 'לא סר ... ימין ושמאל'.
The Eruvin (Bavli) and Yerushalmi passages carry no folio or column in the author's text, and none is added.
וקראת (3:12.94): 'you called' (the pun on Matzref); alternative 'you read'.

Judeo-Arabic, translated from the Arabic as it stands. אר (3:12.235) is read as אד (idh) 'since'. אמנתא (3:12.234) is read amāna 'trustworthy'; alternative amānatinā 'of our faith', as the author's Hebrew has אמונתנו.

Arabic against the author's Hebrew: (1) 'no trustworthy transmission has come down concerning it' against 'we have no tradition concerning it from the sages of our faith' (the Hebrew adds 'from the sages'); (2) 'we can infer' against 'to be drawn from it'; (3) 'or another' against 'or others besides him'; (4) 'forged books ... to some famous scholars' against 'books made for some of the famous sages' (the Arabic has the forged books and says nothing of Rabbi Ishmael in that clause); (5) the Arabic has no 'also'.
patches.reason: Missed allusions and the Arabic-Hebrew differences; the old line said the Arabic 'does not have' what it has and listed too few differences.

And you read his book, Mesharef ha-Emunah.
